prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one 4:3 landscape painting for The Burnt Book Sanskrit learning story. Request 1536 x 1152 native output or the closest supported native 4:3 resolution. Refined Indian watercolor with restrained gouache on warm ivory paper; organic detail, quiet ochre, sage, dusty terracotta, muted indigo. Warm, gentle, evocative storytelling, consistent character design.
Canonical scene brief: The nineteenth statue with a pale blue throat carved into the stone, a faint crescent moon over her brow; Dādī touching the throat and pointing outward; Śuka looking up the hall; Lubdhaka's foreman reading from his notebook.
Character appearances:
you: Always seen from behind or at a distance, face never detailed, so every learner can be the hero: a young person in a simple ochre kurta with a cloth shoulder bag.
dadi: A warm, sharp-eyed grandmother in her seventies, silver hair in a low bun, round spectacles, a cream cotton sari with a thin maroon border and a grey shawl; carries a cloth-bound notebook.
shuka: A bright green rose-ringed parrot with a red beak and a faint pink and black neck ring, a little scruffy, very expressive eyes; usually on your shoulder or Dādī's.
lubdhaka: A tall man in an expensive dark coat over a kurta, rings on his fingers, a leather satchel, usually half in shadow; never monstrous.
malika: A small spirit of rose-coloured sandstone, a young woman wearing a long garland of carved flowers that trails to the floor, each flower a slightly different shape.
Phone-first composition: clear compact narrative grouping, essential faces, hands and objects comfortably inside all edges. Show the complete scene without border. No collage or multi-panel layout.
Owner-approved writing: render the following EXACT text, and no other writing, on the physical surface described in the scene. Use generous size, clear orthographic shapes and accurate Devanagari. The same text remains live app content. Do not substitute, omit, add or invent letters. No watermark, UI or extra labels.
नीलकण्ठः All human and humanoid figures wear complete opaque traditional clothing or robes.

image.brief: The nineteenth statue with a pale blue throat carved into the stone, a faint crescent moon over her brow; Dādī touching the throat and pointing outward; Śuka looking up the hall; Lubdhaka's foreman reading from his notebook.

alt.en: A statue with a pale blue carved throat while an old woman touches it and points outward
alt.hi: हल्के नीले कण्ठ वाली प्रतिमा, उसे छूकर बाहर इशारा करती दादी

narration.en: The nineteenth statue has a pale blue throat carved into the stone. “नीलकण्ठः,” she says. “A blue throat.” “No,” says Dādī. “A karmadhāraya would be the throat itself. This is the one who has the blue throat. The compound points outside itself, to someone else: Śiva. It is called bahuvrīhi, which itself means ‘the one who has much rice’.”
narration.hi: उन्नीसवीं प्रतिमा के पत्थर में हल्का नीला कण्ठ तराशा गया है। “नीलकण्ठः,” वह कहती है। “नीला कण्ठ।” “नहीं,” दादी कहती हैं। “कर्मधारय होता तो वही कण्ठ होता। यह वह है जिसके पास नीला कण्ठ है। समास अपने से बाहर किसी और की ओर संकेत करता है: शिव की ओर। इसे बहुव्रीहि कहते हैं, जिसका अपना अर्थ है ‘बहुत चावल वाला’।”

gloss.en: Moon-faced, with lotus eyes of the finest blue.
gloss.hi: पूर्ण चन्द्र-सा मुख वाली, श्रेष्ठ नील कमल-सी आँखों वाली।

quote.source: Kathāsaritsāgara 1.4 (read in the Digital Corpus of Sanskrit)

body.en: In a {{बहुव्रीहिः}} the whole compound describes a third person: {{नीलः कण्ठः यस्य सः}}, “he whose throat is blue”, is {{नीलकण्ठः}}, Śiva. {{पीतम् अम्बरम् यस्य सः}} is {{पीताम्बरः}}, Viṣṇu. A bahuvrīhi is an adjective, and takes the gender of the person it describes.
body.hi: {{बहुव्रीहिः}} में पूरा समास किसी तीसरे का वर्णन करता है: {{नीलः कण्ठः यस्य सः}}, ‘जिसका कण्ठ नीला है’, {{नीलकण्ठः}} है, शिव। {{पीतम् अम्बरम् यस्य सः}} {{पीताम्बरः}} है, विष्णु। बहुव्रीहि विशेषण है, और वह जिस व्यक्ति का वर्णन करता है उसी का लिंग लेता है।

meaning.en: a compound that describes someone else
meaning.hi: वह समास जो किसी और का वर्णन करता है

caption.hi: बहुव्रीहि स्वामी का नाम बताता है

text.en: the one whose throat is blue (Śiva)

explain.hi: बहुव्रीहि स्वामी का नाम बताता है।

text.en: the one whose throat is blue

prompt.en: Join each compound to its unpacking.
prompt.hi: हर समास को उसके विग्रह से जोड़िए।

explain.hi: हर एक ‘जिसका …’ से शुरू होता है।

prompt.en: Tap every bahuvrīhi (a word naming its owner).
prompt.hi: हर बहुव्रीहि (स्वामी का नाम बताने वाला शब्द) छुइए।

prompt.en: Unpack the compound, then name its kind.
prompt.hi: समास को खोलिए, फिर उसका प्रकार बताइए।

meaning.en: the one whose throat is blue (Śiva)

explain.en: A bahuvrīhi in the feminine, as it describes a woman.
explain.hi: स्त्रीलिंग में बहुव्रीहि, क्योंकि वह स्त्री का वर्णन करता है।

text.en: a woman whose face is like the moon
text.hi: वह स्त्री जिसका मुख चन्द्र-सा है

success.en: “चन्द्रमुखी,” you say, “she whose face is the moon,” and the nineteenth statue lifts her face to the lamplight. The pale blue of her carved throat deepens, from the throat upwards, into the whole stone, and her expression changes, the way a face changes when its name is finally said right. “नीलकण्ठः,” she says. “The one who has it. Yes. I was never the throat. I belong to someone.”
success.hi: “चन्द्रमुखी,” आप कहते हैं, “वह जिसका मुख चन्द्र है,” और उन्नीसवीं प्रतिमा अपना मुख दीपक की रोशनी की ओर उठाती है। उसके तराशे कण्ठ का हल्का नीला रंग गहरा होता है, कण्ठ से ऊपर पूरे पत्थर में, और उसका भाव बदल जाता है, जैसे किसी चेहरे का तब बदलता है जब उसका नाम अन्ततः ठीक कहा जाए। “नीलकण्ठः,” वह कहती है। “वह जिसके पास है। हाँ। मैं कभी कण्ठ नहीं थी। मैं किसी की हूँ।”

failure.en: Her throat stays pale. A bahuvrīhi names the owner: “she whose face is the moon”.
failure.hi: उसका कण्ठ हल्का रहता है। बहुव्रीहि स्वामी का नाम बताता है: ‘वह जिसका मुख चन्द्र है’।

body.en: Sūtra 2.2.23, {{शेषो बहुव्रीहिः}}, calls the remaining compounds {{बहुव्रीहिः}}, and 2.2.24, {{अनेकमन्यपदार्थे}}, says several words join in the sense of another word, someone outside the compound. The compound's own gender and number come from the one it describes.
body.hi: सूत्र 2.2.23, {{शेषो बहुव्रीहिः}}, शेष समासों को {{बहुव्रीहिः}} कहता है, और 2.2.24, {{अनेकमन्यपदार्थे}}, कहता है कि कई शब्द किसी अन्य पद के अर्थ में जुड़ते हैं, अर्थात् समास से बाहर कोई। समास का अपना लिंग और वचन उसी से आता है जिसका वह वर्णन करता है।

text.en: The one in yellow; the ten-faced one.
text.hi: पीले वस्त्र वाला; दस मुख वाला।

text.en: She whose face is the moon.
